# Stargate SG1 | William Joseph Devane (born September 5, 1939) is an American actor | Facebook
## # Stargate SG1 | William Joseph Devane (born September 5, 1939) is an American actor · 223.4K members
In 1994, Devane appeared as Al Capone in Lois & Clark: The New Adventures of Superman in an episode titled "That Old Gang of Mine". He also had a recurring role on the CBS series Early Edition (1996–2000) as the main character's father. Devane appeared in the films McCabe & Mrs. Miller (1971); Lady Liberty (1971); Family Conspiracy (1976), directed by Alfred Hitchcock; Marathon Man (1976); Rolling Thunder (1977); Yanks (1979); Testament (1983) with Jane Alexander; Timestalkers (1987) with Lauren Hutton and Klaus Kinski; Forgotten Sins (1996) with John Shea; Exception to the Rule (1997); Payback (1999); Hollow Man (2000) and Space Cowboys (2000).
Devane played members of the presidential cabinet in two evening dramas. In 2004, he made a guest appearance on The West Wing as Secretary of State and potential candidate for Vice President. Devane appeared in several scenes with Martin Sheen; they also appeared together as President John F. Kennedy and his brother Robert, respectively, 30 years earlier in The Missiles of October (1974). In 2005, he joined the 24-member cast as Secretary of Defense James Heller for seasons four through six.
LATER CAREER

# Stargate SG1 | William Joseph Devane (born September 5, 1939) is an American actor | Facebook
## # Stargate SG1 | William Joseph Devane (born September 5, 1939) is an American actor · 223.4K members
In 2004, Devane appeared in three episodes of Stargate SG-1 as President Henry Hayes and can be seen in the direct-to-DVD film Stargate: Continuum. He also starred in the short-lived sitcom Crumbs and as Brian's real estate agent father in What About Brian (2006–07). In 2008, he appeared in Russ Emanuel's Chasing the Green alongside Jeremy London, Ryan and Robert Picardo. He also appears as police officer and psychologist Dr. Dix appeared in the Jesse Stone mystery films with Tom Selleck. In 2010, he appeared in the NCIS episode "Worst Nightmare" as a grandfather who is not what he seems and is in reality a former U.S -Special agent for a child kidnapped from Marine Corps Base Quantico.
In 2012, Devane began a recurring role as Grandpa Edward Grayson on the ABC primetime soap opera Revenge. [8] Devane also played the President of the United States in Christopher Nolan's film The Dark Knight Rises. Devane reprized his role as James Heller, now President, in the limited series 24: Live Another Day, which premiered in May 2014.
Devane had a guest role as Williams as part of NASA in the 2014 film Interstellar and a year later he was also part of the regular cast of the sitcom The Grinder. In 2022, he appeared in a four-episode guest appearance on the Amazon Prime Video detective series Bosch: Legacy.
PRIVATE LIFE
He married Eugenie "Debbie" McCabe in 1961 and they live in Sherman Oaks, Los Angeles with their two sons: Joshua, who is also an actor, and Bill, who died in an accident at an older age. When time permits, the family travels to their ranch in Utah, where Devane enjoys fly fishing and horseback riding and playing polo with Arabian horses, a sport for which he has won numerous awards.PRIVATE LIFE

## # Stargate SG1 | William Joseph Devane (born September 5, 1939) is an American actor · 223.4K members
In 1994, Devane appeared as Al Capone in Lois & Clark: The New Adventures of Superman in an episode titled "That Old Gang of Mine". He also had a recurring role on the CBS series Early Edition (1996–2000) as the main character's father. Devane appeared in the films McCabe & Mrs. Miller (1971); Lady Liberty (1971); Family Conspiracy (1976), directed by Alfred Hitchcock; Marathon Man (1976); Rolling Thunder (1977); Yanks (1979); Testament (1983) with Jane Alexander; Timestalkers (1987) with Lauren Hutton and Klaus Kinski; Forgotten Sins (1996) with John Shea; Exception to the Rule (1997); Payback (1999); Hollow Man (2000) and Space Cowboys (2000).
Devane played members of the presidential cabinet in two evening dramas. In 2004, he made a guest appearance on The West Wing as Secretary of State and potential candidate for Vice President. Devane appeared in several scenes with Martin Sheen; they also appeared together as President John F. Kennedy and his brother Robert, respectively, 30 years earlier in The Missiles of October (1974). In 2005, he joined the 24-member cast as Secretary of Defense James Heller for seasons four through six.

## # Stargate SG1 | William Joseph Devane (born September 5, 1939) is an American actor · 223.4K members
In 2004, Devane appeared in three episodes of Stargate SG-1 as President Henry Hayes and can be seen in the direct-to-DVD film Stargate: Continuum. He also starred in the short-lived sitcom Crumbs and as Brian's real estate agent father in What About Brian (2006–07). In 2008, he appeared in Russ Emanuel's Chasing the Green alongside Jeremy London, Ryan and Robert Picardo. He also appears as police officer and psychologist Dr. Dix appeared in the Jesse Stone mystery films with Tom Selleck. In 2010, he appeared in the NCIS episode "Worst Nightmare" as a grandfather who is not what he seems and is in reality a former U.S -Special agent for a child kidnapped from Marine Corps Base Quantico.
In 2012, Devane began a recurring role as Grandpa Edward Grayson on the ABC primetime soap opera Revenge. [8] Devane also played the President of the United States in Christopher Nolan's film The Dark Knight Rises. Devane reprized his role as James Heller, now President, in the limited series 24: Live Another Day, which premiered in May 2014.
Devane had a guest role as Williams as part of NASA in the 2014 film Interstellar and a year later he was also part of the regular cast of the sitcom The Grinder. In 2022, he appeared in a four-episode guest appearance on the Amazon Prime Video detective series Bosch: Legacy.
PRIVATE LIFE
He married Eugenie "Debbie" McCabe in 1961 and they live in Sherman Oaks, Los Angeles with their two sons: Joshua, who is also an actor, and Bill, who died in an accident at an older age. When time permits, the family travels to their ranch in Utah, where Devane enjoys fly fishing and horseback riding and playing polo with Arabian horses, a sport for which he has won numerous awards.PRIVATE LIFE

**Marshall R. Teague** (born April 16, 1953) is an American film and television actor known for his balance of starring roles with powerful supporting characters, allowing him to build a varied and pivotal body of work. He was born in Newport, Tennessee. He is of English, French, and Cherokee ancestry. At age nine, he spent time with relatives throughout Asia, where he began a passion for the martial arts training in Korean Kuk Sool Won Hapkido. He holds black belts in both Korean Hapkido and Tae Kwon Do. Marshall joined the U.S. Navy and served in Vietnam. While serving in the 6th Fleet, he won NATO heavyweight kickboxing championship. Upon retiring from military service, Marshall entered the sheriff's department in Shelby County, Tennessee (Memphis). While working undercover, he found acting lessons had become pivotal. In 1978, Marshall moved to Los Angeles, becoming a full-time actor.
His breakout role was as Jimmy Reno in the cult-classic movie _Road House_ and for his recurring role on the 1990s science-fiction series _Babylon 5_ as Ta'Lon, a Narn soldier, and Nelson Drake. He also had several guest roles playing different characters on the TV series _Walker, Texas Ranger_.
Marshall has also appeared in _The Rock_ (1996) and _Armageddon_ (1998), both of which were directed by Michael Bay. He is the only actor to portray Lt. Black Jack Pershing in director John Milius' film _Rough Riders_ and Eduard Shevardnadze, the Soviet Union minister of foreign affairs under Mikhail Gorbachev in director Sean McNamara's film _Reagan_.

Teague's TV guest-star appearances include _Walker, Texas Ranger_, where he has made memorable guest appearances as different characters. He was Walker's first nemesis in the pilot episode "One Riot, One Ranger", "Payback", "Codename: Dragonfly", "Last of a Breed Parts 1 & 2", "Fight or Die", "The Final Showdown 1 and 2" last TV film _Trial by Fire_. He appearanced on _Babylon 5_ as a human in the season-one episode "Infection" and made a guest appearance on the _Babylon 5_ spinoff _Crusade_ as Captain Daniels in the episode "The Long Road". He was in three episodes of the science-fiction TV series _Sliders_ as General Kronos and Sheriff Redfield.
He was a series regular on television in the soap opera_Days of Our Lives_ as Leonard Stacy in 1984, as Brian McCord in 1985, and Colin Lawson in 1989. Also, he was in the soap operas _Generations_ as Officer O’Reilly and _The Bold and the Beautiful_ as Paul 2004. He starred as a series regular on the 1980s HBO series _1st & Ten_ as Mace Petty. He appeared in the action sci-fi (TV series) _Super Force_ as Frank Stone and the military drama _Pensacola: Wings of Gold_ as Major to Colonel Drayton. In the military drama _[Soldier of Fortune, Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soldier\_of\_Fortune,\_Inc. "Soldier of Fortune, Inc.")_, he was David Drummer, and in the 2007 (telenovela) romance drama _American Heiress_, he was Richard Van Aiken.

Teague has made costarring appearances on several popular TV shows, including _Columbo: Uneasy Lies the Crown_, _Stargate SG-1_ episode "A Matter of Time", _The Fall Guy_ (multiple episodes portraying a con man, mob enforcer, car thief), _Automan_, _Knight Rider_, _[Mama's Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's\_Family "Mama's Family")_ episode "[Blackbelt Mama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Mama's_Family_episodes#Season_2_(1983%E2%80%9384) "List of Mama's Family episodes")", a love interest on _Moonlighting_ episode "North by North DiPesto", _She Spies_, _The A-Team_, _Quantum Leap_ episode "How the Tess Was Won", multiple episodes of _MacGyver_, _Renegade_, _Hunter_, _[Who's the Boss?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who's\_the\_Boss%3F "Who's the Boss?")_, _Tales from the Crypt_, _Star Trek: Deep Space Nine_ in the season-four episode "Hippocratic Oath", and on _Star Trek: Voyager_ in the season-three episode "Distant Origin". He also portrayed the real-life love interest (Mike Stone) in Priscilla Presley's biographical story (TV movie) _Elvis & Me_ as character Rick Colten.
In the video game industry, he is known as the voice of Krunk in the video game _Crash Nitro Kart_ and as the model for Captain Elias Walker in _Call of Duty: Ghosts._

**George Stevens Hamilton**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-1) (born August 12, 1939)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-2) is an American actor.
For his debut performance in _[Crime and Punishment U.S.A.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime\_and\_Punishment\_U.S.A. "Crime and Punishment U.S.A.")_ (1959), Hamilton won a Golden Globe Award and was nominated for a BAFTA Award. He has received one additional BAFTA nomination[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-bafta.org-3) and two Golden Globe nominations.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-4) His early career was dominated by dramatic and leading man roles often based on his good looks and debonair style, while later film roles emphasizing more comedic roles and self-depreciating humor. Additionally, Hamilton was a longtime commercial spokesman for Ritz Crackers. According to _Filmink_ "he managed to survive an incredible amount of flops to not only forge an entirely decent career of sixty plus years, but also evolved into a very good actor."[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-ink-5)
Hamilton is known for his deeply tanned appearance, with Bo Derek joking about a competition between Hamilton and her late husband John Derek "as to who had the most tan!"[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-6)

Hamilton was born in Memphis, Tennessee, and spent his early years with his mother, Ann (née Stevens), in Blytheville, Arkansas.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-7) He attended Hawthorne School in Beverly Hills, California.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-mind-8) In 1950, his mother sent him to live with his father in the north.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-mind-8) He briefly attended a progressive school in New York City before being sent to the Gulf Coast Military Academy in Gulfport, Mississippi.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-mind-8)
Hamilton's stepfathers were Carleton Hunt and Jesse Spalding; his stepmother was June Howard, with whom Hamilton said he had repeated sexual relations when he was 12, shortly after she married his father, and again when he was an adult.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-9)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-mind-8)

Hamilton's first roles were in television, appearing in shows such as _The Veil_[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) (playing an Indian), _The Adventures of Rin Tin Tin_, _The Donna Reed Show_,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) and _Cimarron City_. His first film role was a lead, _[Crime and Punishment U.S.A.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime\_and\_Punishment\_U.S.A. "Crime and Punishment U.S.A.")_ (1959),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) directed by Denis Sanders. Hamilton signed a five year contract with Denis and Terry Sanders' TD Productions.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-pact-11)
Hamilton (left) with Lizabeth Scott and host Mike Stokey on Stump the Stars, 1963.

Hamilton's work on _Crime and Punishment_ was seen by MGM who cast him in _Home from the Hill_ (1960) and put the actor under contract.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) He was considered for roles in _The Time Machine_, _Cimarron_, _Mutiny on the Bounty_ and _Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-ink-5) MGM cast Hamilton in support of Natalie Wood and Robert Wagner in the melodrama _All the Fine Young Cannibals_ (1960)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) and the beach party comedy _Where the Boys Are_ (1960).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) Hamilton appeared in the lower budgeted _Angel Baby_ (1961),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) a drama about an evangelist, for Allied Artists, who had to borrow Hamilton from TD Productions.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-pact-11) It had minimal commercial or critical impact. The movie was the feature debut of Burt Reynolds, who recalled "George was different. When I came to Hollywood, there were 175 Marlon Brandos, 2,000 Jimmy Deans, and a lot of Carroll Bakers. But nobody wanted to be David Niven, except George." Reynolds later said, "if anybody could have gotten him to be" as "relaxed and self-deprecating on film" as he was in real life "he would have been the next Cary Grant."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-12)

For United Artists, Hamilton supported Lana Turner in the melodrama _By Love Possessed_ (1961). MGM tried to change his image by putting him in the Western _A Thunder of Drums_ (1961).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) In 1961 Hamilton brought suit against TD Productions but eventually settled out of court saying he would pay them $10,000 per picture for the next seven pictures in five years, exclusive of the ones he made for MGM. Hamilton's contract with TD Productions went to his own company, Ash Productions.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-pact-11)
Hamilton lobbied hard for the role of the Italian husband in _Light in the Piazza_ (1962),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) with Olivia de Havilland. The film lost money, but Hamilton received excellent notices. It was shot in Italy, and MGM kept Hamilton in Italy to play a role in _Two Weeks in Another Town_ (1962).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) Hamilton had a part in _The Victors_ (1963),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) an anti-war drama from Carl Foreman. His performance was described as "excellent".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-pep-13) Hamilton played Moss Hart in _Act One_ (1963),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10)

**Shannen Maria Doherty** (; April 12, 1971 – July 13, 2024) was an American actress.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-ObitNYT-3) During her career in film and television, she played, among others, Jenny Wilder in _Little House on the Prairie_ (1982–1983); Maggie Malene in _Girls Just Want to Have Fun_ (1985); Kris Witherspoon in _Our House_ (1986–1988); Heather Duke in _Heathers_ (1989); Brenda Walsh in _Beverly Hills, 90210_ (1990–1994), _90210_ (2008–2009), and _BH90210_ (2019); Rene Mosier in _Mallrats_ (1995); and Prue Halliwell in _Charmed_ (1998–2001).

## Early life and education
[edit]
Shannen Maria Doherty was born on April 12, 1971,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-4)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-ObitNYT-3) in Memphis, Tennessee,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-5) to Tom and Rosa Doherty. She was raised in her mother's Southern Baptist faith.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-6) Doherty attended the Lycée Français de Los Angeles, a private French-language school, from which she graduated in 1988.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-7)

## Early life and education
### Child acting: 1982–1988
[edit]
In 1982, Doherty had guest spots on TV series including _Voyagers!_ and _Father Murphy_, which was created and produced by Michael Landon. The same year, 11-year-old Doherty won the recurring role of Jenny Wilder on _Little House on the Prairie_,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-8) in which Landon starred and produced.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-Bio-9) Doherty appeared in 18 episodes in the final season of the show, which was cancelled in 1983.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-ObitNYT-3)
Doherty lent her voice to the animated film _The Secret of NIMH_ in 1982. She appeared in an episode of _[Magnum, P.I.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnum,\_P.I. "Magnum, P.I.")_ ("A Sense of Debt"), followed by an early episode of _Airwolf_ ("Bite of the Jackal"), for which she was nominated as Best Young Actress: Guest in a Series at the 6th Youth in Film Awards in 1984.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-10)
In 1985, Doherty starred as Maggie Malene in the teen movie comedy _Girls Just Want to Have Fun_ alongside actresses Helen Hunt and Sarah Jessica Parker. Doherty was cast as the oldest Witherspoon sibling, Kris, on the family drama _Our House_, which ran from 1986 to 1988, a role which garnered her a Young Artist Award nomination.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-11)
Doherty with Jason Priestley at the Governor's Ball following the 43rd Annual Emmy Awards, August 1991

## Early life and education
### Child acting: 1982–1988
Doherty's first major motion picture role was in the dark comedy_Heathers_, which premiered in 1988. She garnered worldwide attention and fame for her breakout role as Brenda Walsh in the Aaron Spelling–produced TV series _Beverly Hills, 90210_ in 1990. In 1991 and 1992, her portrayal of Brenda earned her a Young Artist Award nomination for Best Young Actress Starring in a Television Series.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-Young_Artist_Awards-12) Doherty left the show after the fourth season in 1994.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-ObitNYT-3)
She appeared nude in _Playboy_ magazine, first in December 1993, followed by a spread in March 1994.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-13) She posed for the magazine again in December 2003 and was featured in a 10-page pictorial.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-15)

## Early life and education
### Child acting: 1982–1988
Doherty's career afterward primarily consisted of made-for-TV movies, although she also had a lead role in Kevin Smith's 1995 film _Mallrats_ and later cameoed in _Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back_. In 1998, Spelling again cast her in another of his television series, _Charmed_, in which she played one of the lead characters, Prue Halliwell, the oldest of three sisters who are witches. Doherty also directed three episodes for the series during the second and third seasons, including the western special "The Good, the Bad and the Cursed".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-16) Doherty left the show in 2001 at the end of the third season, resulting in her character's death in the episode "All Hell Breaks Loose" which she directed. Reportedly, her departure was caused by on-set and off-set tensions between Doherty and co-star Alyssa Milano.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-y645-17) In 2004, E! placed Doherty at number 10 on their list of the _50 Most Wicked Women of Prime Time_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-g520-18) In 2007, AOL named Prue Halliwell the 9th greatest witch in television history.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-AOL_TV-19)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannen_Doherty#cite_note-20)

**Marshall R. Teague** (born April 16, 1953) is an American film and television actor known for his balance of starring roles with powerful supporting characters, allowing him to build a varied and pivotal body of work. He was born in Newport, Tennessee. He is of English, French, and Cherokee ancestry. At age nine, he spent time with relatives throughout Asia, where he began a passion for the martial arts training in Korean Kuk Sool Won Hapkido. He holds black belts in both Korean Hapkido and Tae Kwon Do. Marshall joined the U.S. Navy and served in Vietnam. While serving in the 6th Fleet, he won NATO heavyweight kickboxing championship. Upon retiring from military service, Marshall entered the sheriff's department in Shelby County, Tennessee (Memphis). While working undercover, he found acting lessons had become pivotal. In 1978, Marshall moved to Los Angeles, becoming a full-time actor.
His breakout role was as Jimmy Reno in the cult-classic movie _Road House_ and for his recurring role on the 1990s science-fiction series _Babylon 5_ as Ta'Lon, a Narn soldier, and Nelson Drake. He also had several guest roles playing different characters on the TV series _Walker, Texas Ranger_.
Marshall has also appeared in _The Rock_ (1996) and _Armageddon_ (1998), both of which were directed by Michael Bay. He is the only actor to portray Lt. Black Jack Pershing in director John Milius' film _Rough Riders_ and Eduard Shevardnadze, the Soviet Union minister of foreign affairs under Mikhail Gorbachev in director Sean McNamara's film _Reagan_.

Teague's TV guest-star appearances include _Walker, Texas Ranger_, where he has made memorable guest appearances as different characters. He was Walker's first nemesis in the pilot episode "One Riot, One Ranger", "Payback", "Codename: Dragonfly", "Last of a Breed Parts 1 & 2", "Fight or Die", "The Final Showdown 1 and 2" last TV film _Trial by Fire_. He appearanced on _Babylon 5_ as a human in the season-one episode "Infection" and made a guest appearance on the _Babylon 5_ spinoff _Crusade_ as Captain Daniels in the episode "The Long Road". He was in three episodes of the science-fiction TV series _Sliders_ as General Kronos and Sheriff Redfield.
He was a series regular on television in the soap opera_Days of Our Lives_ as Leonard Stacy in 1984, as Brian McCord in 1985, and Colin Lawson in 1989. Also, he was in the soap operas _Generations_ as Officer O’Reilly and _The Bold and the Beautiful_ as Paul 2004. He starred as a series regular on the 1980s HBO series _1st & Ten_ as Mace Petty. He appeared in the action sci-fi (TV series) _Super Force_ as Frank Stone and the military drama _Pensacola: Wings of Gold_ as Major to Colonel Drayton. In the military drama _[Soldier of Fortune, Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soldier\_of\_Fortune,\_Inc. "Soldier of Fortune, Inc.")_, he was David Drummer, and in the 2007 (telenovela) romance drama _American Heiress_, he was Richard Van Aiken.
texts.2:
Teague has made costarring appearances on several popular TV shows, including _Columbo: Uneasy Lies the Crown_, _Stargate SG-1_ episode "A Matter of Time", _The Fall Guy_ (multiple episodes portraying a con man, mob enforcer, car thief), _Automan_, _Knight Rider_, _[Mama's Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's\_Family "Mama's Family")_ episode "[Blackbelt Mama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Mama's_Family_episodes#Season_2_(1983%E2%80%9384) "List of Mama's Family episodes")", a love interest on _Moonlighting_ episode "North by North DiPesto", _She Spies_, _The A-Team_, _Quantum Leap_ episode "How the Tess Was Won", multiple episodes of _MacGyver_, _Renegade_, _Hunter_, _[Who's the Boss?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who's\_the\_Boss%3F "Who's the Boss?")_, _Tales from the Crypt_, _Star Trek: Deep Space Nine_ in the season-four episode "Hippocratic Oath", and on _Star Trek: Voyager_ in the season-three episode "Distant Origin". He also portrayed the real-life love interest (Mike Stone) in Priscilla Presley's biographical story (TV movie) _Elvis & Me_ as character Rick Colten.
In the video game industry, he is known as the voice of Krunk in the video game _Crash Nitro Kart_ and as the model for Captain Elias Walker in _Call of Duty: Ghosts._

**George Stevens Hamilton**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-1) (born August 12, 1939)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-2) is an American actor.
For his debut performance in _[Crime and Punishment U.S.A.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime\_and\_Punishment\_U.S.A. "Crime and Punishment U.S.A.")_ (1959), Hamilton won a Golden Globe Award and was nominated for a BAFTA Award. He has received one additional BAFTA nomination[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-bafta.org-3) and two Golden Globe nominations.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-4) His early career was dominated by dramatic and leading man roles often based on his good looks and debonair style, while later film roles emphasizing more comedic roles and self-depreciating humor. Additionally, Hamilton was a longtime commercial spokesman for Ritz Crackers. According to _Filmink_ "he managed to survive an incredible amount of flops to not only forge an entirely decent career of sixty plus years, but also evolved into a very good actor."[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-ink-5)
Hamilton is known for his deeply tanned appearance, with Bo Derek joking about a competition between Hamilton and her late husband John Derek "as to who had the most tan!"[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-6)
texts.1:
Hamilton was born in Memphis, Tennessee, and spent his early years with his mother, Ann (née Stevens), in Blytheville, Arkansas.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-7) He attended Hawthorne School in Beverly Hills, California.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-mind-8) In 1950, his mother sent him to live with his father in the north.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-mind-8) He briefly attended a progressive school in New York City before being sent to the Gulf Coast Military Academy in Gulfport, Mississippi.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-mind-8)
Hamilton's stepfathers were Carleton Hunt and Jesse Spalding; his stepmother was June Howard, with whom Hamilton said he had repeated sexual relations when he was 12, shortly after she married his father, and again when he was an adult.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-9)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-mind-8)
texts.2:
Hamilton's first roles were in television, appearing in shows such as _The Veil_[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) (playing an Indian), _The Adventures of Rin Tin Tin_, _The Donna Reed Show_,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) and _Cimarron City_. His first film role was a lead, _[Crime and Punishment U.S.A.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime\_and\_Punishment\_U.S.A. "Crime and Punishment U.S.A.")_ (1959),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) directed by Denis Sanders. Hamilton signed a five year contract with Denis and Terry Sanders' TD Productions.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-pact-11)
Hamilton (left) with Lizabeth Scott and host Mike Stokey on Stump the Stars, 1963.
texts.3: Hamilton's work on _Crime and Punishment_ was seen by MGM who cast him in _Home from the Hill_ (1960) and put the actor under contract.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) He was considered for roles in _The Time Machine_, _Cimarron_, _Mutiny on the Bounty_ and _Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-ink-5) MGM cast Hamilton in support of Natalie Wood and Robert Wagner in the melodrama _All the Fine Young Cannibals_ (1960)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) and the beach party comedy _Where the Boys Are_ (1960).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) Hamilton appeared in the lower budgeted _Angel Baby_ (1961),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) a drama about an evangelist, for Allied Artists, who had to borrow Hamilton from TD Productions.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-pact-11) It had minimal commercial or critical impact. The movie was the feature debut of Burt Reynolds, who recalled "George was different. When I came to Hollywood, there were 175 Marlon Brandos, 2,000 Jimmy Deans, and a lot of Carroll Bakers. But nobody wanted to be David Niven, except George." Reynolds later said, "if anybody could have gotten him to be" as "relaxed and self-deprecating on film" as he was in real life "he would have been the next Cary Grant."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-12)
texts.4:
For United Artists, Hamilton supported Lana Turner in the melodrama _By Love Possessed_ (1961). MGM tried to change his image by putting him in the Western _A Thunder of Drums_ (1961).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) In 1961 Hamilton brought suit against TD Productions but eventually settled out of court saying he would pay them $10,000 per picture for the next seven pictures in five years, exclusive of the ones he made for MGM. Hamilton's contract with TD Productions went to his own company, Ash Productions.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-pact-11)
Hamilton lobbied hard for the role of the Italian husband in _Light in the Piazza_ (1962),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) with Olivia de Havilland. The film lost money, but Hamilton received excellent notices. It was shot in Italy, and MGM kept Hamilton in Italy to play a role in _Two Weeks in Another Town_ (1962).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) Hamilton had a part in _The Victors_ (1963),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10) an anti-war drama from Carl Foreman. His performance was described as "excellent".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-pep-13) Hamilton played Moss Hart in _Act One_ (1963),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Hamilton_(actor)#cite_note-tv-10)

### The former Chicago cop brought a gritty authenticity to every role, and thrived in both dramas and comedies. A familiar television presence since the 1980s, he was most recently seen on the Fox comedy _New Girl_.

Dennis Farina, who spent 18 years with the Chicago Police Department before devoting himself to acting in the 1980s, died July 22, 2013, in Scottsdale, Arizona. He was 69.
According to news reports, the cause was a blood clot in a lung.
Farina, who earned his first acting credits while still working as a Chicago detective, made numerous films and was a regular cast member or guest star on many television series.
His best known movies included _Get Shorty_, _Midnight Run_, _Saving Private Ryan_, _Out of Sight_ and _Snatch_.
On television, he starred in such series as _Crime Story_, _The In-Laws_, _Buddy Faro_, _Law & Order_ and _Luck_, and had recurring or guest roles in many others, including, _Hardcastle and McCormick_, _Hunter_, _China Beach_, _Miami Vice_ and, most recently, _New Girl_, in which he played the father of Jake Johnson's character, Nick.
He also appeared in numerous made-for-TV movies, such as _The Case of the Hillside Stranglers_, _People Like Us_, _Drug Wars: The Cocaine Cartel_, _A Stranger in the Mirror_, _The Corpse Had a Familiar Face_, _Bella Mafia_ and _Empire Falls_.
Farina was a favorite of writer-director Michael Mann, a fellow Chicagoan who met Farina when, as a police officer, he served as Mann's tour guide during the making of the feature film _Thief_. Mann was so taken by Farina that he cast him in the film, and in many other TV and movie projects, including _Crime Story_, _Manhunter_, _Hunter_, _Miami Vice_, _Drug Wars: The Cocaine Cartel_ and _Luck_.

# Dennis Farina, Prolific Character Actor for More Than 30 Years
### The former Chicago cop brought a gritty authenticity to every role, and thrived in both dramas and comedies. A familiar television presence since the 1980s, he was most recently seen on the Fox comedy _New Girl_.
Born in Chicago to Sicilian-American parents on February 29, 1944, Farina graduated from St. Michael's Central High School. He then served three years in the U.S. Army and went on to join the police force and study criminal justice at Truman Junior College.
In a statement, Lori DeWaal, Farina's longtime publicist, said, "We are deeply saddened by the loss of a great actor and a wonderful man. Dennis Farina was always warmhearted and professional, with a great sense of humor and passion for his profession. He will be greatly missed by his family, friends and colleagues. We hope that he finds a new life where great roles are plentiful and the Cubs are always winning the pennant. We ask that the press refrain from contacting his family at this time so that they can mourn their loss together.”
Dick Wolf, creator of _Law & Order_, said, "I was stunned and saddened to hear about Dennis’ unexpected passing this morning. The _Law & Order_ family extends sympathy and condolences to his family. He was a great guy.”

Title: Ken Osmond
Chunks: 4,5,6,7,8,9,10,11,12
After _Leave It to Beaver_ ended in 1963, Osmond continued to make occasional appearances on such television series as CBS's _Petticoat Junction_, _The Munsters_, and a final return appearance on _Lassie_ in the episode "A Matter of Seconds" (1967) as a motorcycle delivery man who offers the hitchhiking collie a lift in his sidecar. He was cast in the feature films _[C'mon Let's Live a Little](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C'mon\_Let's\_Live\_a\_Little "C'mon Let's Live a Little")_ (1967) and _With Six You Get Eggroll_ (1968). However, he found himself typecast as Eddie Haskell and had difficulty finding steady work.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_Stu_Show-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Herald-Journal-5) In 2008, Osmond told radio host Stu Shostak in a radio interview, "I was very much typecast. It's a death sentence. In Hollywood you get typecast. I'm not complaining because Eddie's been too good to me, but I found work hard to come by. In 1968, I bought my first house, in '69 I got married, and we were going to start a family and I needed a job, so I went out and signed up for the LAPD."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_Stu_Show-3)
Osmond during his time in the LAPD, after he survived a shooting

In 1970, Osmond joined the Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD) and grew a mustache in an effort to remain relatively anonymous among citizens, though not among his co-workers.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_Stu_Show-3)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-BillOReilly.com-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_Milwaukee_Journal-10) He worked as a motorcycle officer.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_Victoria_Advocate-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_Deseret_News-12)

On September 20, 1980, Osmond was struck by three bullets while in a foot chase with a suspected car thief.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Herald-Journal-5)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_New_York_Times-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Daily_News_of_Los_Angeles-14) He was protected from two of the bullets by his bullet-resistant vest, with the third bullet ricocheting off his belt buckle.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Herald-Journal-5)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_New_York_Times-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Daily_News_of_Los_Angeles-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_Miami_News_2-15) The shooting was later dramatized in a November 1992 episode of the CBS series _Top Cops_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_Spokesman-Review-16) Osmond applied for a disability pension in 1984, but after an evidentiary hearing in 1986, the Los Angeles Board of Pension Commissioners denied his request by a 4–2 vote.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Indeterminate-17) Osmond appealed the determination to the Superior Court and in 1988 a judge overturned the Board's denial and awarded Osmond a lifetime pension, and he retired from the force.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-18)

In 1983, Osmond appeared as a game show participant and celebrity guest star on the _Match Game-Hollywood Squares Hour_, along with _Beaver_ co-stars Jerry Mathers, Richard Deacon and Jeri Weil. Osmond returned to acting in 1983 reprising his role as Eddie Haskell in the CBS made-for-television movie _Still the Beaver_, which followed the adult Cleaver boys, their friends, and their families.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Herald-Journal-5)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_Milwaukee_Journal-10)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Observer-Reporter-19) The television movie was a success and led to the revival comedy series _The New Leave It to Beaver_, which premiered the following year.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_Milwaukee_Journal-10)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Miami_Herald-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Chicago_Tribune-21) The show ran for four seasons from 1984 to 1989, starting on The Disney Channel, and later moving to WTBS.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Miami_Herald-20)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Reading_Eagle-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Gadsden_Times-23) On the show, Osmond played Eddie Haskell as a husband and father, while his character's two sons, Freddie Haskell and Edward "Bomber" Haskell Jr., were played by Osmond's two real-life sons, Eric Osmond and Christian Osmond.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_Stu_Show-3)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Reading_Eagle-22)

In 1987, Osmond was honored by the Young Artist Foundation with its Former Child Star "Lifetime Achievement" Award for his role as Eddie Haskell.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-YoungArtistAwards.org-24) He continued to make television appearances throughout the 1980s and 1990s on the shows _Happy Days_ and _Rags to Riches_, and the television movie _[High School U.S.A.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High\_School\_U.S.A. "High School U.S.A.")_,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Youngstown_Vindicator_2-25) as well as cameo appearances as Eddie Haskell on such television shows as _[Parker Lewis Can't Lose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parker\_Lewis\_Can't\_Lose "Parker Lewis Can't Lose")_ and _[Hi Honey, I'm Home!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hi\_Honey,\_I'm\_Home! "Hi Honey, I'm Home!")_. In the 1997 feature film _Leave It to Beaver_, Osmond played Eddie Haskell Sr., and Adam Zolotin played his son Eddie Haskell Jr.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_Stu_Show-3) He also had a bit part in the 2016 indie movie _Characterz_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Reed-26)

In 1969, Osmond married Sandra Purdy.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_Stu_Show-3)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Ancestry.com-27) They had two sons, Eric E. Osmond and Christian S. Osmond.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_Stu_Show-3)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Herald-Journal-5)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Reading_Eagle-22) Following his retirement from the police force, Osmond handled rental properties in Los Angeles County and made occasional personal appearances at film festivals, collectors' shows, and nostalgia conventions.
On September 18, 2007, Osmond filed a class action lawsuit against the Screen Actors Guild, alleging that SAG had collected $8 million in foreign residuals for U.S. actors but had not distributed them to the actors.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_Hollywood_Reporter-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Variety-30) SAG settled the lawsuit in 2010, providing $7.9 million in royalties to actors.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-31)
Osmond was the co-author, along with Christopher J. Lynch, of the book _Eddie: The Life and Times of America's Preeminent Bad Boy_, which was published in September 2014. The foreword was written by Jerry Mathers.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-32)

Osmond died at his home in Los Angeles on May 18, 2020, at age 76, from complications of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and peripheral artery disease.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-nyt1-4)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Reed-26)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-33) News of his death was first announced by his son Eric in a statement through Osmond's representative.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Reed-26)
In the early 1970s, a story was widely reported that Osmond had become rock star Alice Cooper. According to Cooper, the rumor began when a college newspaper editor asked him what kind of kid he was, to which Cooper replied, "I was obnoxious, disgusting, a real Eddie Haskell." However, the story ended up reporting that Cooper was the real Eddie Haskell. Cooper would later tell the _New Times_, "It was the biggest rumor that ever came out about me. Finally, I got a T-shirt that said 'No, I am not Eddie Haskell.' But people still believed it."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_Miami_News-7)

Another widely reported urban legend of the 1970s was that Osmond had grown up to become adult film star John Holmes.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Beaver_County_Times-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Anchorage_Daily_News-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Boca_Raton_News-36) The story apparently began when fan magazines falsely reported that Osmond had embarked on such a career. The rumor was dispelled when a Los Angeles movie theater lit up its marquee advertising "Eddie Haskell of TV in _'Behind the Green Door'_– X-rated", prompting Osmond himself, then an LAPD officer, to go to the theater to request that the manager remove his character's name from the marquee.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-37) Osmond testified at his disability hearing in 1986 that in 1971 he was called into LAPD Internal Affairs and asked to disrobe to prove he was not John Holmes.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Indeterminate-17)
In the early 1980s, Osmond sued an adult bookstore in Los Angeles called Le Sex Shoppe, which was selling an adult video starring Holmes. The video advertised that the film featured "'Little Eddie Haskell' from 'Leave it to Beaver.'" Osmond claimed that the film's advertising defamed him, but the trial court dismissed the case and Osmond appealed to the California Court of Appeals, which also ruled against him, stating that there was no evidence that the owner of the bookstore was aware of the defamatory language on the packaging and therefore had not acted with "malice" in selling the video.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-38)

Osmond died at his home in Los Angeles on May 18, 2020, at age 76, from complications of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and peripheral artery disease.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-nyt1-4)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Reed-26)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-33) News of his death was first announced by his son Eric in a statement through Osmond's representative.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Reed-26)
In the early 1970s, a story was widely reported that Osmond had become rock star Alice Cooper. According to Cooper, the rumor began when a college newspaper editor asked him what kind of kid he was, to which Cooper replied, "I was obnoxious, disgusting, a real Eddie Haskell." However, the story ended up reporting that Cooper was the real Eddie Haskell. Cooper would later tell the _New Times_, "It was the biggest rumor that ever came out about me. Finally, I got a T-shirt that said 'No, I am not Eddie Haskell.' But people still believed it."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-The_Miami_News-7)
texts.11:
Another widely reported urban legend of the 1970s was that Osmond had grown up to become adult film star John Holmes.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Beaver_County_Times-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Anchorage_Daily_News-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Boca_Raton_News-36) The story apparently began when fan magazines falsely reported that Osmond had embarked on such a career. The rumor was dispelled when a Los Angeles movie theater lit up its marquee advertising "Eddie Haskell of TV in _'Behind the Green Door'_– X-rated", prompting Osmond himself, then an LAPD officer, to go to the theater to request that the manager remove his character's name from the marquee.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-37) Osmond testified at his disability hearing in 1986 that in 1971 he was called into LAPD Internal Affairs and asked to disrobe to prove he was not John Holmes.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-Indeterminate-17)
In the early 1980s, Osmond sued an adult bookstore in Los Angeles called Le Sex Shoppe, which was selling an adult video starring Holmes. The video advertised that the film featured "'Little Eddie Haskell' from 'Leave it to Beaver.'" Osmond claimed that the film's advertising defamed him, but the trial court dismissed the case and Osmond appealed to the California Court of Appeals, which also ruled against him, stating that there was no evidence that the owner of the bookstore was aware of the defamatory language on the packaging and therefore had not acted with "malice" in selling the video.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Osmond#cite_note-38)

# Dennis Farina, Prolific Character Actor for More Than 30 Years
### The former Chicago cop brought a gritty authenticity to every role, and thrived in both dramas and comedies. A familiar television presence since the 1980s, he was most recently seen on the Fox comedy _New Girl_.

Dennis Farina, who spent 18 years with the Chicago Police Department before devoting himself to acting in the 1980s, died July 22, 2013, in Scottsdale, Arizona. He was 69.
According to news reports, the cause was a blood clot in a lung.
Farina, who earned his first acting credits while still working as a Chicago detective, made numerous films and was a regular cast member or guest star on many television series.
His best known movies included _Get Shorty_, _Midnight Run_, _Saving Private Ryan_, _Out of Sight_ and _Snatch_.
On television, he starred in such series as _Crime Story_, _The In-Laws_, _Buddy Faro_, _Law & Order_ and _Luck_, and had recurring or guest roles in many others, including, _Hardcastle and McCormick_, _Hunter_, _China Beach_, _Miami Vice_ and, most recently, _New Girl_, in which he played the father of Jake Johnson's character, Nick.
He also appeared in numerous made-for-TV movies, such as _The Case of the Hillside Stranglers_, _People Like Us_, _Drug Wars: The Cocaine Cartel_, _A Stranger in the Mirror_, _The Corpse Had a Familiar Face_, _Bella Mafia_ and _Empire Falls_.
Farina was a favorite of writer-director Michael Mann, a fellow Chicagoan who met Farina when, as a police officer, he served as Mann's tour guide during the making of the feature film _Thief_. Mann was so taken by Farina that he cast him in the film, and in many other TV and movie projects, including _Crime Story_, _Manhunter_, _Hunter_, _Miami Vice_, _Drug Wars: The Cocaine Cartel_ and _Luck_.

# Dennis Farina, Prolific Character Actor for More Than 30 Years
### The former Chicago cop brought a gritty authenticity to every role, and thrived in both dramas and comedies. A familiar television presence since the 1980s, he was most recently seen on the Fox comedy _New Girl_.
Born in Chicago to Sicilian-American parents on February 29, 1944, Farina graduated from St. Michael's Central High School. He then served three years in the U.S. Army and went on to join the police force and study criminal justice at Truman Junior College.
In a statement, Lori DeWaal, Farina's longtime publicist, said, "We are deeply saddened by the loss of a great actor and a wonderful man. Dennis Farina was always warmhearted and professional, with a great sense of humor and passion for his profession. He will be greatly missed by his family, friends and colleagues. We hope that he finds a new life where great roles are plentiful and the Cubs are always winning the pennant. We ask that the press refrain from contacting his family at this time so that they can mourn their loss together.”
Dick Wolf, creator of _Law & Order_, said, "I was stunned and saddened to hear about Dennis’ unexpected passing this morning. The _Law & Order_ family extends sympathy and condolences to his family. He was a great guy.”

Johnson's first major role was in the 1969 stage production of _[Fortune and Men's Eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortune\_and\_Men's\_Eyes "Fortune and Men's Eyes")_, in which he played the lead role of Smitty.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-Loder-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-14) The play was produced and directed by Sal Mineo at the Coronet Theatre in Los Angeles.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-15) It included a "shockingly realistic prison rape" scene portrayed by Johnson.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-16) This exposure led to the quickly forgotten film _The Magic Garden of Stanley Sweetheart_ (1970). Johnson continued to work on stage, film and television without breaking into stardom. His notable films from this period were _Zachariah_ (1971), _Lollipop and Roses_ (1971), _The Harrad Experiment_ (1973) (a film in which Johnson displayed frontal nudity)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-18) and _A Boy and His Dog_ (1975). In 1976, Johnson was the roommate of Sal Mineo at the time Mineo was murdered.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-19)

### _Miami Vice_ and stardom
[edit]
Johnson in 1986
In 1984, after years of struggling to establish himself as a TV actor, Johnson landed a starring role as undercover police detective Sonny Crockett in the Michael Mann/Universal Television cop series, _Miami Vice_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-20) The show ran from 1984 to 1990.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-21)_Miami Vice_ made Johnson "a major international star".[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-22) According to _Rolling Stone_, "No one had more swagger in the Reagan era than Don Johnson. As _Miami Vice_'s Sonny Crockett, the undercover detective and professional stubble-cultivator who lived on a houseboat with his pet alligator Elvis, he embodied masculine cool in the era of coke binges and Lamborghinis".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-23) The Sonny Crockett character typically wore thousand-dollar Versace and Armani suits over pastel cotton T-shirts, drove a Ferrari, wore expensive timepieces by Rolex and Ebel, and lived on an Endeavour yacht.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-27)_Miami Vice_ was noted for its revolutionary use of music and cinematography,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-28) and for its glitzy take on the police drama genre.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-29) In the show, Crockett's partner was Ricardo Tubbs, played by Philip Michael Thomas.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-30)

### _Miami Vice_ and stardom
Johnson's work on _Miami Vice_ earned him a Golden Globe Award for Best Performance by an Actor in a Television Series – Drama, in 1986.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-31) He was nominated for the same award in 1987.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-32) He was also nominated for a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series in 1985.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-34)
Between seasons on _Miami Vice_, Johnson gained further renown through the TV miniseries _The Long Hot Summer_ (1985), a remake of the 1958 film.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-35) During the time he was on _Miami Vice_, he had set up an hour-long music video/pay cable program with videocassette versions of the programs Johnson had hosted being handled by distributor CBS/Fox Video. The project was a tie-in to his first album _Heartbeat_, which was released by CBS/Epic Records in 1986.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-36)
In 1988, he starred in the romantic comedy _Sweet Hearts Dance_, alongside Susan Sarandon, Jeff Daniels and Elizabeth Perkins.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-37) In 1989 he played the sheriff of Los Angeles County Jerry Beck in John Frankenheimer's film _Dead Bang_.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-38)

### _Miami Vice_ and stardom
In the early 1990s, Johnson played a variety of roles in well-produced films, including the role of drifter and car salesman Harry Maddox in Dennis Hopper's _The Hot Spot_ (1990) opposite Jennifer Connelly and Virginia Madsen.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-39) He worked on two films with his wife Melanie Griffith, _Paradise_ (1991) and _Born Yesterday_ (1993).[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-41) He appeared alongside Mickey Rourke in _Harley Davidson and the Marlboro Man_ (1991),[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-42) and in Sidney Lumet's thriller _Guilty as Sin_ (1993), opposite Rebecca De Mornay.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-43)
Johnson later starred in the 1996–2001 CBS-TV police drama _Nash Bridges_ with Cheech Marin, Jeff Perry, Jaime P. Gomez, Kelly Hu, Wendy Moniz, [Annette O'Toole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_O'Toole "Annette O'Toole"), [Jodi Lyn O'Keefe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodi_Lyn_O'Keefe "Jodi Lyn O'Keefe") as his daughter Cassidy, and James Gammon as his father Nick. Johnson portrayed the title role, an inspector (later promoted to captain) for the San Francisco Police Department. In _Nash Bridges_, Johnson was again paired with a flashy convertible car, a yellow 1971 Plymouth Barracuda.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-44)
Don Johnson with Demi Moore and Ashton Kutcher at the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2006

texts.4: Johnson's first major role was in the 1969 stage production of _[Fortune and Men's Eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortune\_and\_Men's\_Eyes "Fortune and Men's Eyes")_, in which he played the lead role of Smitty.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-Loder-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-14) The play was produced and directed by Sal Mineo at the Coronet Theatre in Los Angeles.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-15) It included a "shockingly realistic prison rape" scene portrayed by Johnson.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-16) This exposure led to the quickly forgotten film _The Magic Garden of Stanley Sweetheart_ (1970). Johnson continued to work on stage, film and television without breaking into stardom. His notable films from this period were _Zachariah_ (1971), _Lollipop and Roses_ (1971), _The Harrad Experiment_ (1973) (a film in which Johnson displayed frontal nudity)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-18) and _A Boy and His Dog_ (1975). In 1976, Johnson was the roommate of Sal Mineo at the time Mineo was murdered.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-19)
texts.5:
### _Miami Vice_ and stardom
[edit]
Johnson in 1986
In 1984, after years of struggling to establish himself as a TV actor, Johnson landed a starring role as undercover police detective Sonny Crockett in the Michael Mann/Universal Television cop series, _Miami Vice_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-20) The show ran from 1984 to 1990.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-21)_Miami Vice_ made Johnson "a major international star".[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-22) According to _Rolling Stone_, "No one had more swagger in the Reagan era than Don Johnson. As _Miami Vice_'s Sonny Crockett, the undercover detective and professional stubble-cultivator who lived on a houseboat with his pet alligator Elvis, he embodied masculine cool in the era of coke binges and Lamborghinis".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-23) The Sonny Crockett character typically wore thousand-dollar Versace and Armani suits over pastel cotton T-shirts, drove a Ferrari, wore expensive timepieces by Rolex and Ebel, and lived on an Endeavour yacht.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-27)_Miami Vice_ was noted for its revolutionary use of music and cinematography,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-28) and for its glitzy take on the police drama genre.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-29) In the show, Crockett's partner was Ricardo Tubbs, played by Philip Michael Thomas.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-30)
texts.6:
### _Miami Vice_ and stardom
Johnson's work on _Miami Vice_ earned him a Golden Globe Award for Best Performance by an Actor in a Television Series – Drama, in 1986.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-31) He was nominated for the same award in 1987.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-32) He was also nominated for a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series in 1985.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-34)
Between seasons on _Miami Vice_, Johnson gained further renown through the TV miniseries _The Long Hot Summer_ (1985), a remake of the 1958 film.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-35) During the time he was on _Miami Vice_, he had set up an hour-long music video/pay cable program with videocassette versions of the programs Johnson had hosted being handled by distributor CBS/Fox Video. The project was a tie-in to his first album _Heartbeat_, which was released by CBS/Epic Records in 1986.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-36)
In 1988, he starred in the romantic comedy _Sweet Hearts Dance_, alongside Susan Sarandon, Jeff Daniels and Elizabeth Perkins.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-37) In 1989 he played the sheriff of Los Angeles County Jerry Beck in John Frankenheimer's film _Dead Bang_.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-38)
texts.7:
### _Miami Vice_ and stardom
In the early 1990s, Johnson played a variety of roles in well-produced films, including the role of drifter and car salesman Harry Maddox in Dennis Hopper's _The Hot Spot_ (1990) opposite Jennifer Connelly and Virginia Madsen.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-39) He worked on two films with his wife Melanie Griffith, _Paradise_ (1991) and _Born Yesterday_ (1993).[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-41) He appeared alongside Mickey Rourke in _Harley Davidson and the Marlboro Man_ (1991),[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-42) and in Sidney Lumet's thriller _Guilty as Sin_ (1993), opposite Rebecca De Mornay.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-43)
Johnson later starred in the 1996–2001 CBS-TV police drama _Nash Bridges_ with Cheech Marin, Jeff Perry, Jaime P. Gomez, Kelly Hu, Wendy Moniz, [Annette O'Toole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annette_O'Toole "Annette O'Toole"), [Jodi Lyn O'Keefe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodi_Lyn_O'Keefe "Jodi Lyn O'Keefe") as his daughter Cassidy, and James Gammon as his father Nick. Johnson portrayed the title role, an inspector (later promoted to captain) for the San Francisco Police Department. In _Nash Bridges_, Johnson was again paired with a flashy convertible car, a yellow 1971 Plymouth Barracuda.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Johnson#cite_note-44)
Don Johnson with Demi Moore and Ashton Kutcher at the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2006

**Roger Cross** (born 19 October 1969) is a Jamaican actor. He is known for his work as Curtis Manning on _24_ (2005–2007) and Detective Donovan McAvoy in _Coroner_ (2019-2022). He earned a Canadian Screen Award nomination for Best Lead Actor in a drama series for _Coroner_ and the show was nominated for Best Drama Series, 2020.
Cross also has other television roles that include _First Wave_ (1998–2001), _Arrow_ (2012), _Continuum_ (2012–2015), _Motive_ (2013–2016), _Dark Matter_ (2015–2017), _Murdoch Mysteries_ (2023-2024) _Sight Unseen_ (2024-present). In film, He voiced John Stewart and Swamp Thing in the DC Animated Movie Universe films _Justice League Dark_ (2017) and _Justice League Dark: Apokolips War_ (2020). He also voiced Ulysses in the _Lonesome Road_ expansion of the post-apocalyptic video game _Fallout: New Vegas_ (2010).

Cross was born in Christiana, Jamaica.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-black-1) When he was eleven, his family emigrated to Canada, settling in Vancouver, British Columbia.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-black-1) He graduated with a degree in Aviation and General Studies from Trinity Western University.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-black-1) Before his acting career, Cross was a professional pilot.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-buddy-2)
Cross began his career in the 1990s playing guest roles in such series as _Street Justice_, _The X-Files_, _Sliders_, _Stargate SG-1_, _Highlander: The Series_, _Relic Hunter_, _The 4400_, _Higher Ground_, _Star Trek: Enterprise_, and _Chuck_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-shaw-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-sci-4)
He auditioned for the role of [Teal'c](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teal'c "Teal'c") in Stargate SG-1, but lost out to Christopher Judge.
From 1998 to 2001, he starred as a lead character, Joshua Bridges, on the sci-fi series_First Wave._[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-morton-5)
From 2005 to 2007, Cross achieved wider recognition for his role as CTU Agent Curtis Manning on the Fox television drama _24_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-buddy-2)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-6) In 2009, he appeared as DJ and drag queen Sunset Boulevard/Sonny Benson in the Showtime series _The L Word_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-7)

In 2010, Cross did voice-over work as Ulysses in the _Fallout: New Vegas_ add-ons Old World Blues and Lonesome Road.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-btva-8)
Cross's other notable television roles include Staff Sergeant Boyd Bloom in _Motive_, Detective Lucas Hilton in _Arrow_, Reggie Fitzwilliam in _The Strain_, Travis Verta in _Continuum_, and Six in _Dark Matter_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-eh-9)
In addition to his work on television, Cross has appeared in such films as _The Chronicles of Riddick_, _X2_, _Ballistic: Ecks vs. Sever_, _Beautiful Joe_, _Free Willy 3: The Rescue_, _World Trade Center_, _Re-Kill_, and _Mad Money._[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-11)
Cross is in a long-term relationship with actress and yoga instructor Josephine Jacob. They have two sons,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-black-1) Kaniel Jacob-Cross and actor Gabriel Jacob-Cross, whose appearances include _The Man in the High Castle_ (2015) and _Snowpiercer_ (2020).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-13)

Title: Dominic Kalipersad on Instagram: "Did you know that three leading actors in the 1990s US TV series The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air were of Trinidadian descent?

Alfonso Ribeiro, Tatyana Ali, and Karyn Parsons portrayed all three of the Banks children.

Alfonso Ribeiro: 
Born Sept. 21, 1971, in NYC in the U.S.  to Trinidadian parents Joy Ribeiro and Michael Ribeiro, (and the paternal grandson of Trinidadian calypsonian Albert Ribeiro, known as Lord Hummingbird), he began his career at age 8, but is probably best known for his most prominent role as Carlton Banks, the cousin of Will Smith’s lead character on “Fresh Prince” from Sept. 1990 to May 1996.

Tatyana Ali:
Born on Jan. 24, 1979, in the US to a Sheriff Ali, a retired police officer from Trinidad, and Sonia Ali, a nurse from Panama, she is a Harvard graduate. She began her career in entertainment at the age of four, appearing on the children’s television show Sesame Street. In 1990, Ali landed the role of Ashley Banks on “Fresh Prince”, which launched her into stardom.

Karyn Parsons:
Born Oct. 8, 1966, to a Trinidadian mother, Louise (Hankerson) Parsons, and a French-Canadian father, Kenneth B. Parsons, she had her first TV role in the NBC drama The Bronx Zoo (1987), but she made her big break as Will Smith’s cousin, Hilary Banks, on The Fresh Prince of Bell Air.

There were other actors in guest starring roles, including Nia Long whose maternal grandparents were from Trinidad.

In “Fresh Prince”, Long portrayed the role of  Lisa Wilkes who almost married Will Smith.

#thefreshprinceofbelair #actorswithtriniroots

**Roger Cross** (born 19 October 1969) is a Jamaican actor. He is known for his work as Curtis Manning on _24_ (2005–2007) and Detective Donovan McAvoy in _Coroner_ (2019-2022). He earned a Canadian Screen Award nomination for Best Lead Actor in a drama series for _Coroner_ and the show was nominated for Best Drama Series, 2020.
Cross also has other television roles that include _First Wave_ (1998–2001), _Arrow_ (2012), _Continuum_ (2012–2015), _Motive_ (2013–2016), _Dark Matter_ (2015–2017), _Murdoch Mysteries_ (2023-2024) _Sight Unseen_ (2024-present). In film, He voiced John Stewart and Swamp Thing in the DC Animated Movie Universe films _Justice League Dark_ (2017) and _Justice League Dark: Apokolips War_ (2020). He also voiced Ulysses in the _Lonesome Road_ expansion of the post-apocalyptic video game _Fallout: New Vegas_ (2010).
texts.1:
Cross was born in Christiana, Jamaica.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-black-1) When he was eleven, his family emigrated to Canada, settling in Vancouver, British Columbia.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-black-1) He graduated with a degree in Aviation and General Studies from Trinity Western University.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-black-1) Before his acting career, Cross was a professional pilot.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-buddy-2)
Cross began his career in the 1990s playing guest roles in such series as _Street Justice_, _The X-Files_, _Sliders_, _Stargate SG-1_, _Highlander: The Series_, _Relic Hunter_, _The 4400_, _Higher Ground_, _Star Trek: Enterprise_, and _Chuck_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-shaw-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-sci-4)
He auditioned for the role of [Teal'c](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teal'c "Teal'c") in Stargate SG-1, but lost out to Christopher Judge.
From 1998 to 2001, he starred as a lead character, Joshua Bridges, on the sci-fi series_First Wave._[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-morton-5)
From 2005 to 2007, Cross achieved wider recognition for his role as CTU Agent Curtis Manning on the Fox television drama _24_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-buddy-2)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-6) In 2009, he appeared as DJ and drag queen Sunset Boulevard/Sonny Benson in the Showtime series _The L Word_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-7)
texts.2:
In 2010, Cross did voice-over work as Ulysses in the _Fallout: New Vegas_ add-ons Old World Blues and Lonesome Road.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-btva-8)
Cross's other notable television roles include Staff Sergeant Boyd Bloom in _Motive_, Detective Lucas Hilton in _Arrow_, Reggie Fitzwilliam in _The Strain_, Travis Verta in _Continuum_, and Six in _Dark Matter_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-eh-9)
In addition to his work on television, Cross has appeared in such films as _The Chronicles of Riddick_, _X2_, _Ballistic: Ecks vs. Sever_, _Beautiful Joe_, _Free Willy 3: The Rescue_, _World Trade Center_, _Re-Kill_, and _Mad Money._[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-11)
Cross is in a long-term relationship with actress and yoga instructor Josephine Jacob. They have two sons,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-black-1) Kaniel Jacob-Cross and actor Gabriel Jacob-Cross, whose appearances include _The Man in the High Castle_ (2015) and _Snowpiercer_ (2020).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cross#cite_note-13)

There were other actors in guest starring roles, including Nia Long whose maternal grandparents were from Trinidad.
In “Fresh Prince”, Long portrayed the role of Lisa Wilkes who almost married Will Smith.

**Helen Dorothy Martin** (July 23, 1909 – March 25, 2000)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Martin#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Martin#cite_note-3) was an American actress of stage and television. Martin's career spanned over 60 years, appearing first on stage and later in film and television. Martin is best known for her roles as Wanda Williams on the CBS sitcom _Good Times_ (1974–1979) and as Pearl Shay on the NBC sitcom _227_ (1985–1990).

### Early life and education
[edit]
Martin was born in St. Louis and raised in Nashville, Tennessee.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Martin#cite_note-Playbill-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Martin#cite_note-JET1-5) She was an only child born to a family of musicians.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Martin#cite_note-collier-6) Martin's parents wanted their daughter to become a concert pianist.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Martin#cite_note-collier-6) At the urging of her parents, Martin attended Fisk University for a two-year span before dropping out to embark on an acting career.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Martin#cite_note-7) During the Great Depression, Martin supported herself as a domestic worker.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Martin#cite_note-collier-6)
After leaving college, Martin moved to Chicago, and New York City thereafter to study acting with the WPA Theater and the Rose McClendon Players. She was a founding member of the American Negro Theater in Harlem.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Martin#cite_note-nyt_2000-8) Martin became a Broadwaycharacter actress for many decades, debuting in 'Orchids Preferred' in 1937 and thereafter Orson Welles's production of _Native Son_ in 1941.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Martin#cite_note-Playbill-4)
Martin appeared in a dozen Broadway shows, including Jean Genet's _The Blacks_, the musical _Raisin_ from 1973 until 1975, Ossie Davis's _Purlie Victorious_ (and later the musical version, which was called _Purlie_), _The Amen Corner_ and Tennessee Williams's _Period of Adjustment_.

### Early life and education
Martin became widely known later in life due to her roles in popular television series, which brought her a large audience. She had a recurring role as Wanda "Weeping Wanda" Williams on the television series _Good Times_, and later as the neighbor Pearl Shay on the television sitcom _227_, which lasted from 1985 until 1990. Martin also had a role on the short-lived sitcoms _[Baby, I'm Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby,\_I'm\_Back "Baby, I'm Back")_ (as mother in-law, Luzelle)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Martin#cite_note-9) and _[That's My Mama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That's\_My\_Mama "That's My Mama")_. Martin portrayed a variety of grandmothers in films: _Hollywood Shuffle_ (1987),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Martin#cite_note-10)_[Don't Be a Menace to South Central While Drinking Your Juice in the Hood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't\_Be\_a\_Menace\_to\_South\_Central\_While\_Drinking\_Your\_Juice\_in\_the\_Hood "Don't Be a Menace to South Central While Drinking Your Juice in the Hood")_ (1996), _I Got the Hook Up_ (1998),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Martin#cite_note-11)_House Party 2_ (1991), and Mama Doll in _Bulworth_ (1998).

### Early life and education
While appearing on _[Late Night with Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late\_Night\_with\_Conan\_O'Brien "Late Night with Conan O'Brien")_ to promote _Don't Be a Menace_, Martin sent host [Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_O'Brien "Conan O'Brien") and the audience into a frenzy with her remark, "I love reefer!" in response to a question about being cast as a pot-smoking grandmother in the film. She also said she would have been a stripper had she not gone into acting and followed her statement with a suggestive dance.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Martin#cite_note-conan-12)
Martin died of a heart attack on March 25, 2000, in Monterey, California, at the age of 90.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Martin#cite_note-JET1-5)
